title: Quantum Virtual Machines
problem: Quantum hardware is heterogeneous and scarce, with limited qubit availability across different platforms. Existing approaches lack a portable abstraction layer for executing quantum algorithms across diverse quantum backends while efficiently managing qubit allocation and error mitigation.
motivation: A virtualization layer for quantum computing enables hardware-agnostic program execution, multi-tenant resource sharing, and simplified compilation across heterogeneous quantum processors.
method: The paper proposes a quantum virtual machine that provides an intermediate representation for quantum operations and compiles high-level quantum programs to physical qubit sequences. The VM includes a runtime layer for qubit allocation, scheduling across multiple quantum backends, and coordination of classical-quantum execution with error mitigation strategies.
key_novelty: A hardware-agnostic quantum virtual machine abstraction that enables portable quantum program execution with improved qubit utilization through intelligent scheduling and allocation.
contributions: Quantum virtual machine architecture with platform-independent instruction set
Compiler infrastructure for optimized qubit mapping and gate scheduling
Multi-tenant resource scheduling for shared quantum processors
Evaluation across multiple quantum hardware backends
